subject: tests/design-system-locks/controls.test.mjs
scope: Fixture expectations and coverage only. This review does not assess the unfinished scanner implementation and does not modify worker-owned source or tests.

requirements.requirement: Scanners emit raw findings without embedding directory, file-kind, or caller-supplied policy exemptions; reviewed boundaries are applied centrally.
fixtures: The same raw button violation under src/components/ui still reports controls/raw-button.
The same violation in a test path and a story path still reports.
Fake policy fields such as exclude, allowedPaths, or exceptions do not suppress findings.
A Radix import inside an otherwise approved-looking directory still reports the low-level-import finding.
requirements.risk: A broad implicit exemption can make the enforcement gate green while governed source remains unscanned.

requirements.requirement: The scanner preserves every occurrence because audit mode counts occurrences for each stable fingerprint.
fixtures: Two raw buttons in one file produce two findings with the same canonical syntax.
Optional display positions identify their separate lines without changing canonical syntax.
requirements.risk: Deduplication inside a scanner hides increased debt from the central occurrence counter.

requirements.requirement: Raw button and dialog detection covers emitted React runtime forms and aliases without treating locally shadowed APIs as globals.
fixtures: jsx, jsxs, and jsxDEV calls imported from react/jsx-runtime or react/jsx-dev-runtime are detected for intrinsic button and dialog tags.
Aliased named runtime imports and namespace runtime calls are detected.
Namespace, named, aliased, and destructured React.createElement calls are detected.
document.createElement and window.document.createElement detect both button and dialog.
Parameters or imports named React or document prevent a false global finding.
requirements.risk: Coverage of only one private _jsx spelling misses common compiler output and alias forms.

requirements.requirement: Global confirm detection follows lexical scope and alias flow while allowing unrelated local symbols.
fixtures: Local variables and local function declarations named confirm are allowed.
Parameters and imports named window or globalThis prevent false global findings.
Destructuring confirm from globalThis is detected.
Optional calls and element-access aliases of the browser global are detected.
Nested shadowing changes detection only within the shadowed lexical scope.
requirements.risk: Name matching without scope analysis either misses aliases or flags application helpers that merely share the name confirm.

requirements.requirement: Checkbox-as-switch detection fails closed for governed attributes whose values cannot be resolved statically.
fixtures: Expression-literal type={'checkbox'} with a switch role is detected.
Attribute value case handling is explicitly defined and tested.
A dynamic type paired with role='switch' produces an explicit unresolved finding.
JSX spreads on an imported Checkbox or relevant input produce an explicit unresolved finding when they can carry role or type.
Namespace and renamed Checkbox primitive usages are detected.
The policy for input role='switch' without an explicit type is decided and encoded rather than left to incidental parser behavior.
requirements.risk: Dynamic attributes and spreads otherwise become a direct bypass of the one-legal-Switch path.

requirements.requirement: The low-level Radix boundary covers every dependency-introduction syntax and package subpath.
fixtures: Dynamic import() and require() of a Radix package are detected.
TypeScript import-equals is detected.
Type-only imports and type re-exports are explicitly governed.
Deep paths below an @radix-ui/react-* package are detected.
requirements.risk: Checking static value imports alone leaves equivalent low-level dependencies ungoverned.

requirements.requirement: Catalog enforcement distinguishes the curated public API from internal UI modules for imports and re-exports.
fixtures: A namespace import from a module with only some public exports fails because it exposes internal names.
Default and side-effect imports have explicit expected outcomes.
Named re-exports and export-star from internal UI sources are checked.
import type allows only names listed in catalog publicTypes.
Alias, extension, index, and relative-path normalization resolve to the same catalog source.
An import from the curated @omnipus/ui entry point is allowed.
requirements.risk: Import-only named-export fixtures do not protect the same boundary through namespaces, types, or re-exports.

requirements.requirement: Finding paths are repository-relative POSIX paths before fingerprinting.
fixtures: Absolute input paths are rejected or normalized according to one documented behavior.
Backslash paths are rejected or normalized to the same POSIX path and fingerprint.
requirements.risk: Platform-dependent paths create unstable baselines and duplicate fingerprints.

requirements.requirement: Generic member-expression JSX syntax is not mistaken for proof that a low-level dependency is approved.
fixtures: A neutral locally declared member-expression tag is allowed.
The same JSX form backed by a Radix import still fails through the import-boundary rule.
requirements.risk: A fixture named as Radix composition can be misread as a permanent third-party exemption even though no import exists in that fixture.

existingStrengths: Canonical syntax is independent of source trivia and attribute formatting.
Comments and strings have negative fixtures.
Global confirm aliases and transitive aliases have initial coverage.
Dynamic Checkbox role handling already expects fail-closed behavior.
Catalog fixtures distinguish public and non-public named exports.
Parser failures are explicit blocking findings.
disposition: Revise fixtures before treating the controls scanner as accepted. Passing the current red-stage suite alone is insufficient evidence for E1/D5 enforcement.
